 TOI Tech Desk / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Nov 20, 2026, 12:59 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print Elon Musk Just hours before Anthropic started trading on the Nasdaq in what became one of the largest AI IPOs on record, fresh disclosures revealed that Elon Musk 's business empire could be one of the biggest beneficiaries of the company's growth, despite his public criticism of the Claude maker earlier this year. According to Moneywise report, Anthropic’s IPO filling revealed that the company agreed to spend up to $120.5 billion on compute infrastructure from SpaceX AI, the AI division of Musk-led SpaceX, through agreements that extend into 2029. The revelation emerged months after Musk publicly attacked Anthropic, accusing its AI chatbot Claude of bias and describing the company as "misanthropic and evil." Anthropic's blockbuster IPO
 Claude-maker Anthropic made its blockbuster debut on Wall Street with the company’s valuation reaching nearly $2 trillion. Shares of the company closed at $97.17, up by 17% from its IPO price of $83. Soon after the debut, Anthropic shared a statement from CEO Dario Amodei reaffirming the company’s core focus on safety, committing to pace AI training and deployment as needed to maintain human control while resisting business or political pressures, framing this as essential to avoid risks like misuse or loss of control. “Today puts the company in a stronger financial position, and in doing so only strengthens our resolve to do the right thing,” Amodei said. “If we can show it’s possible to make the right choices on safety and still build an incredibly successful company, others in our industry will be inspired to do the same. We call this a race to the top,” he added. From public criticism to major business partner
 SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has been one of the most vocal critics of Anthropic this year. In February, after Anthropic announced a $30 billion funding round at a $380 billion valuation, the billionaire took aim at the company on X. "Your AI hates Whites & Asians, especially Chinese, heterosexuals and men," Musk wrote at the time. "This is misanthropic and evil. Fix it." In a separate post, Musk also mocked the company's name, suggesting there was irony in Anthropic becoming "misanthropic. " However, newly disclosed IPO paperwork shows that even as Musk criticised Anthropic publicly, business ties between the two companies were expanding rapidly behind the scenes. $120.5 billion compute agreement
 The S-1 filling on Anthropic revealed that the company is committed to spending up to $120.5 billion with SpaceXAI for computing power used to train and run advanced AI systems. For the uninitiated, Compute has become one of the most important and valuable resource in the artificial intelligence industry, encompassing specialised Nvidia chips, data-centre capacity and power infrastructure necessary to develop increasingly powerful AI models. The filing further suggests that once all contracted capacity is delivered, then Claude-maker Anthropic could be spending around $3.1 billion per month on compute services from SpaceXAI. Partnership expanded after May deal
 The relationship between the two companies appears to have accelerated shortly after Musk's criticism. In May this year, Anthropic announced that it would utilise the full computing capacity of SpaceX’s Colossus 1 data centre in Memphis, Tennessee. The facility reportedly included more than 300 megawatts of power and over 220,000 Nvidia GPUs dedicated to AI workloads. Subsequent agreements signed between May and October significantly increased Anthropic's commitment to SpaceX-owned infrastructure. Bloomberg previously reported that Anthropic had become SpaceX's largest revenue source, accounting for a substantial portion of the company's third-quarter revenue. Deal includes exit clauses
 Despite the eye-catching $120.5 billion figure, the agreements do not guarantee the entire amount will be spent. According to the IPO filing, both parties have the right to terminate portions of the arrangement after initial non-cancellable periods expire in early 2027. Following those periods, either company can end the agreements with 90 days' written notice. Analysts have noted that future compute prices could influence whether Anthropic maintains the full commitment. Falling prices may encourage Anthropic to seek cheaper alternatives, while rising prices could prompt suppliers to renegotiate terms. AI infrastructure costs continue to soar
 The SpaceXAI agreement is only one piece of Anthropic's massive infrastructure spending plans. The company's amended IPO filing disclosed roughly $900.9 billion in total commitments, the vast majority tied to compute capacity and AI infrastructure. Join conversation

 The disclosures underscore the enormous costs associated with building next-generation AI models and explain why access to chips, power and data centres has become a strategic battleground between leading AI companies. For Musk, the filings reveal a striking contrast between his public attacks on Anthropic and the growing business relationship between the two firms. While Grok and Claude remain rivals in the race to build advanced AI systems, Anthropic's IPO documents show that one of its biggest suppliers is controlled by the very entrepreneur who once branded the company "misanthropic and evil."
